observations: Theorem 2 states: 'The only H satisfying the three above assumptions is of the form: H = -K Σ_{i=1}^n p_i log p_i', where K is a positive constant.
The entropy for two possibilities with probabilities p and q = 1−p is given by H = −(p log p + q log q).
Figure 7 plots H (in bits) as a function of p, showing a symmetric concave curve peaking at p = 0.5 with H = 1.0 bit.
Two properties of H are listed: (1) H = 0 iff all p_i but one are zero (certainty); (2) H is maximized and equals log n when all p_i are equal (i.e., 1/n).
A footnote references R. C. Tolman, Principles of Statistical Mechanics, Oxford, Clarendon, 1938.
